A-Assertions: Fix assumption regarding description of task in Task.java
commitResults.messageBody:
It is assumed that the description of a task is never null
because the description is checked by the parser before it is passed
to the constructor of Task.

Using assertion will help to catch any unexpected null description and
helps to ensure that the coordination between the parser and the Task
class is working as expected.

Let's use assertion to check that the description of the task is not null
and for it to raise an AssertionError if the description is null.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Assertions: Fix assumption on due date in Deadline class
commitResults.messageBody:
After the the due date is passed into the constructor of the Deadline
class, it is assumed that the 'by' field is set to a value that is not
null because the due date is parsed. If the due date were null, a
JudeyException would be thrown.

Using assertion will help us catch if the exception catches all
instances of due dates being null or invalid. This ensures that after
the due date is parsed, the 'by' field is not null.

Let's add an assertion to check that the 'by' field is not null after
parsing the due date in the Deadline class constructor.
This will help us identify any potential issues during development and
testing.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Assertions: Fix assumption on from and to fields in Event class
commitResults.messageBody:
Similar to the Deadline class, the from and to values in the paramaters
of the constructor of the Event class are parsed first. It is assumed
that during the parsing if 'from' or 'to' is null, a JudeyException will
be thrown.

Using assertions, we can confirm if the from and to fields are not null
after parsing.

Let's add assertions to check if the from and to values are null after
parsing in the constructor of the Event class. This will help catch any
unexpected null values and ensure that the Event object is created
with valid date and time values.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-CodeQuality: Refactor task classes and parser to improve code quality
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.java and Event.java duplicate date-time parsing logic and
constants, creating maintenance overhead if the date format changes.
Storage.java and task classes use raw string literals for task types
and status markers, which risks silent data corruption upon typos.
Parser.parse() is a monolithic, long method that mixes command
dispatching with low-level string parsing and validation, violating
the Single Level of Abstraction Principle (SLAP).

Let's,
* extract duplicated date-time parsing logic into a new DateTimeUtil
  class
* replace raw magic strings with shared named constants across
  Storage and task classes
* refactor Parser.parse() by extracting dedicated private helper
  methods for each command type to streamline dispatching
A-CodeQuality: Refactor task classes and parser to improve code quality

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Personality: Enhance Judey UI with neon space-cat styling
commitResults.messageBody:
Judey's interface lacks a cohesive visual identity and the chat text
needs stronger readability.

Add a dark space-themed interface with neon arcade styling, astronaut-cat
artwork, improved message bubbles, starfield effects, and bolder
typography.

Keep command syntax, validation, task behavior, and storage compatibility
unchanged so the update improves presentation without affecting existing
users.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-BetterGui: Improve GUI feedback and lifecycle
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI provides limited guidance for malformed commands and does not clearly distinguish the user from Judey.

These limitations make command correction and conversation flow less intuitive.

Add highlighted correction templates, distinct error styling, corrected event-format guidance, a human astronaut user avatar, and delayed GUI shutdown after bye.

Keep command syntax and task storage behavior unchanged while preserving the existing dialog layout for ordinary messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Assertions: Merge assertion fixes into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Task classes assume descriptions and date fields are always present, which can cause unsafe access when malformed data is encountered.

These assumptions make task creation and storage loading vulnerable to runtime failures.

Merge the assertion fixes for task descriptions, deadline dates, and event start/end fields into master.

Keep the existing command behavior while making invalid task data fail through the application's normal validation path.

The user guide needs clearer instructions for running Judey and using its commands.

Let's expand the guide with:
* JAR setup and release-page instructions
* quick-start examples and command summaries
* command formatting rules and expected outcomes
* help, exit, and task persistence explanations
* navigation links and a common-problems table

Rename the default task file to data/judey.txt so the application and
user guide use the same storage location.

The task manager needs a way to locate existing tasks by their descriptions.

Add case-insensitive multi-word searching with helpful validation, preserve original task numbers in results, and document the command in the help text and user guide. Add parser, task-list, and CLI test-plan coverage so the behavior is clear and reusable.

Include the intentional dialog highlight color update with the related UI changes.

commitResults.messageBody: Provide command-specific corrections for missing and invalid task numbers and events-on dates while preserving storage and task-list behavior. Update parser, UI-plan, documentation, and platform-portable output tests.
